cards.name: Variable frame step
cards.summary: Every per-second rate in the flight code is multiplied by one shared elapsed-time scalar, clamped to a narrow band.
cards.behavior: A single shared scalar holds the elapsed seconds since the previous update. It is rebuilt from the graphics frame timer before each update and clamped so that it never falls below the lower bound and never exceeds the upper bound; the storage is also preloaded with a fixed default so the first frame cannot integrate a zero-length step. Physics code multiplies accelerations, angular rates and fuel burn by this scalar, so a drop in frame rate cannot change an integrated trajectory by more than the clamp allows, but the same trajectory will differ slightly between a fast and a slow frame because the step is not fixed. A companion helper moves a value toward a target by at most a rate multiplied by the same scalar and snaps exactly onto the target when the remaining distance drops under a tiny epsilon, which is how every control axis in the game is smoothed without overshoot.

constants.name: Minimum frame step
constants.unit: seconds per update, lower clamp of the elapsed-time scalar

constants.name: Maximum frame step
constants.unit: seconds per update, upper clamp of the elapsed-time scalar

constants.name: Approach snap epsilon
constants.unit: value units, dimensionless dead zone of the rate-limited approach helper; the helper is timestep-aware but this epsilon is not

capabilities: one shared elapsed-time scalar for every integrator
clamped variable timestep between two fixed bounds
rate-limited approach with exact snap
piecewise linear curve lookup for speed and stick gains

cards.name: Airspeed lift
cards.summary: Vertical lift comes from the vertical part of the local air movement, squared, gain-scaled and clamped.
cards.behavior: The model first measures how much of the local air movement crosses the wing by taking the vertical component of the air-velocity difference expressed in body space. That scalar is squared and multiplied by a fixed gain to become an angular push about the pitch axis, so doubling the vertical airspeed quadruples the response and a light updraft produces almost nothing. The result is clamped between a small negative floor and a large positive ceiling so a single violent gust cannot flip the craft instantly. Above a high altitude the whole term fades linearly to zero across a fixed height band, which caps the usable ceiling without an invisible wall. Any surviving roll input multiplies the term down by a factor built from the square root of the bank angle, so a steeply banked wing generates less of this push, and a nose-down attitude diverts a quarter of the same term into the vertical rate instead. A separate coefficient table keyed on angle of attack supplies the wing's inherent effectiveness: it rises steeply through the small positive angles, peaks and holds through the middle of the range, then collapses toward a low plateau at extreme angles including large negative ones.

constants.name: Vertical airspeed lift gain
constants.unit: radians per second squared per (world unit per second) squared of vertical airspeed, applied once per update before the frame step

constants.name: Lift term floor
constants.unit: radians per second squared, lower clamp applied once per update

constants.name: Lift term ceiling
constants.unit: radians per second squared, upper clamp applied once per update

constants.name: Ceiling fade start altitude
constants.unit: world units of height; static threshold, no timestep

constants.name: Ceiling fade band
constants.unit: world units of height over which lift reaches zero; static threshold, no timestep

constants.name: Bank attenuation
constants.unit: multiplier per square root of the bank angle in radians, applied to the lift term once per update

constants.name: Peak wing coefficient
constants.unit: dimensionless coefficient at the peak of the angle-of-attack table; static table entry, no timestep

capabilities: lift proportional to the square of vertical airspeed
symmetric clamp on the lift response
altitude ceiling expressed as a linear fade
bank angle reduces lift authority
angle-of-attack coefficient table

cards.name: Speed-squared drag
cards.summary: Drag grows with airspeed on both axes, is divided back above a reference speed, and includes a component form that is switched off at low speed.
cards.behavior: The wing keeps a separate velocity record for the air it is flying through. Each update it builds a pitch-axis damping term from the vertical and forward components of that relative airspeed offset by a gravity reference, scaled by a fixed coefficient, with the sign following the direction of the relative flow. A yaw-axis term uses the horizontal pair with a slightly smaller coefficient. Both terms are divided by the ratio of current airspeed to a reference speed whenever that ratio exceeds one, and the divisor is capped at two, so above the reference speed drag stops growing faster than the speed itself and the craft settles into a terminal glide. The pitch term is forced to zero while the wing is stalled. A third, smaller term applies a constant times the square of each airspeed component with the sign preserved, which adds a directional damping that is independent of the flow direction; the forward contribution of that term is skipped entirely below a low-speed cutoff, which is what keeps a slow descent from pitching the nose over. A reference-speed lookup additionally scales the first term, holding full strength up to a moderate speed and falling away to nothing by a high speed.

constants.name: Pitch drag coefficient
constants.unit: 1/second applied to the vertical relative airspeed, once per update

constants.name: Yaw drag coefficient
constants.unit: 1/second applied to the horizontal relative airspeed, once per update

constants.name: Drag reference speed
constants.unit: world units per second; above it drag is divided by airspeed over this value

constants.name: Drag divisor cap
constants.unit: dimensionless cap on the airspeed-over-reference divisor, applied once per update

constants.name: Component drag constant
constants.unit: radians per second squared for each (world unit per second) squared of a velocity component, applied once per update

constants.name: Component drag speed cutoff
constants.unit: world units per second, below which the forward component contributes no drag

constants.name: Lateral airspeed roll coupling
constants.unit: radians per second squared per (world unit per second) squared of lateral airspeed, applied once per update

capabilities: separate drag on the pitch and yaw axes
drag divided by airspeed above a reference speed
capped divisor so drag saturates
component drag disabled for the forward axis at low speed
speed-keyed drag scaling table

cards.name: Bank into turn
cards.summary: Stick input becomes a bank angle that then produces yaw, and a shoulder button holds a steep bank without stick pressure.
cards.behavior: Raw stick axes pass through a shaping curve and then into two rate-limited approach helpers, one per axis, so commanded bank and pitch track the stick smoothly instead of jumping. The lateral command becomes an angular impulse about the yaw axis proportional to half of the wing's lateral extent, and that term is cut to three tenths while a boost input is held, which makes a banked turn wider under boost. A second impulse about the roll axis uses a larger fixed gain against the same lateral extent, so the visual bank always leads the heading change and the craft appears to carve. Yaw and roll rates are pulled toward zero by the same approach helper at a fixed decay rate each update, so releasing the stick levels the wing. A shoulder button pair adds a discrete step of about half a radian per press toward a larger held deflection, and a second press extends it further, which lets the pilot hold a steep spiral without continuous stick pressure. The altitude-dependent damping passes through the wings as well, so a high-speed dive damps the roll axis harder than the yaw axis.

constants.name: Yaw impulse gain
constants.unit: radians per second squared per unit of airspeed times bank share, applied once per update

constants.name: Roll impulse gain
constants.unit: radians per second squared per unit of airspeed times bank share, applied once per update

constants.name: Lateral extent share
constants.unit: fraction of the wing's lateral matrix extent used to scale the yaw impulse; static, no timestep

constants.name: Boost bank attenuation
constants.unit: multiplier on the lateral extent while the boost input is held; static, no timestep

constants.name: Stick approach rate
constants.unit: 1/second on both stick axes, applied with the 0.01-0.1 s frame step

constants.name: Shoulder bank step
constants.unit: radians of held bank target added per shoulder-button press; static target, no timestep

capabilities: shaped stick axes with rate-limited tracking
bank converted into yaw impulse
larger roll gain so the bank leads the turn
discrete held bank steps on a shoulder button
boost reduces turn authority

cards.name: Stall and recovery
cards.summary: Stall latches below one airspeed and clears only above a higher one, with a ramped lift share and a gated display warning.
cards.behavior: Airspeed drives a stall flag with hysteresis. The flag sets when airspeed falls under a low threshold and clears only once speed climbs back over a threshold three times higher, so the wing cannot flutter across the boundary in a marginal glide. While speed sits inside a warning band the lift-share value ramps linearly from full authority at the lower edge to none at the upper edge, so control decays instead of vanishing in a single step. A ground clearance under a fifth of a world unit also clears the flag, which prevents a grounded craft from reading as stalled. While the flag is set the pitch-derived drag term is suppressed and the airspeed fade reduces the lift contribution, so the craft mushes forward instead of stalling abruptly. The heads-up display raises a stall warning only when airspeed is under a display threshold, the model is not stalled, no boost input is held, the craft is at least four world units above the ground, the model is in its free-flight state and no other warning already fills the message slot; a second, softer message fires when the flag is already set.

constants.name: Stall entry speed
constants.unit: world units per second of airspeed; static threshold, no timestep

constants.name: Stall exit speed
constants.unit: world units per second of airspeed; static threshold, no timestep

constants.name: Lift ramp top speed
constants.unit: world units per second of airspeed, top of the linear lift-share ramp

constants.name: Stall entry ramp width
constants.unit: world units per second of airspeed between full and zero lift share

constants.name: Warning display speed
constants.unit: world units per second, threshold for the heads-up stall warning

constants.name: Warning minimum altitude
constants.unit: world units above the ground, minimum clearance for the heads-up stall warning; static, no timestep

capabilities: hysteresis latch between two airspeeds
linear ramp of lift share between them
ground clearance clears the stall flag
stall suppresses the pitch drag term
two-stage heads-up stall warning

cards.name: Touchdown gate
cards.summary: A landing counts only when the craft is slow and low over a pad, or inside a strip corridor aligned with the approach.
cards.behavior: Each landing pad stores its own acceptance radius and each landing strip stores a shorter radius plus a separate alignment tolerance. The query walks the pads first, records the smallest planar distance to any of them and marks an index when the craft is inside that pad's radius. It then walks the strips: inside the strip radius it projects the craft position onto the strip axis and rejects the strip when the position falls outside either end plane, otherwise it measures the perpendicular offset from the axis and accepts the strip when that offset is under half the stored alignment tolerance. The strip path reports a sentinel index so the caller can tell a corridor landing apart from a pad landing, and the two outcomes produce different messages. The touchdown state itself additionally requires airspeed under one and a half world units per second and ground clearance under a fifth of a world unit, so a fast pass across the zone never scores. A very large number is returned when nothing at all is near, which keeps the caller's nearest-distance bookkeeping simple.

constants.name: Pad acceptance radius
constants.unit: world units of planar distance stored per landing pad; static, no timestep

constants.name: Strip corridor half-width share
constants.unit: fraction of the stored strip alignment tolerance used as the corridor half-width; static, no timestep

constants.name: Touchdown maximum speed
constants.unit: world units per second; static gate, no timestep

constants.name: Touchdown maximum clearance
constants.unit: world units above the ground surface; static gate, no timestep

constants.name: Far sentinel distance
constants.unit: world units returned when no pad or strip is near; static sentinel, no timestep

capabilities: per-pad acceptance radius
strip corridor with end-plane rejection
perpendicular offset against a half tolerance
sentinel index distinguishes corridor from pad
airspeed and clearance gate on the touchdown
far sentinel for nearest-distance bookkeeping

cards.name: Thruster thrust, gravity and drag
cards.summary: Body-space thrust fights standard gravity and a quadratic drag, and a lost attitude seeds a random tumble.
cards.behavior: The thruster keeps body-space linear and angular velocities that are integrated once per frame step. A downward acceleration of standard gravity magnitude is rotated into body space and added to the linear accumulator, so a pitched or banked craft converts part of gravity into a slide. While the thrust input is held a positive acceleration is applied along the model's local forward axis, and the pitch and roll attitudes contribute lateral accelerations that curve the flight path, which is how the craft steers without a rudder. A quadratic drag pass subtracts a coefficient times each velocity component times that component's own magnitude, so doubling a component quadruples its drag and the vehicle reaches a natural terminal velocity. Angular rates are damped toward zero by a rate-limited approach helper, with separate rates for pitch and roll versus yaw. When attitude control is lost the model multiplies the whole velocity by a fixed negative share and, only while the residual angular rate is still under a small angle, seeds a random tumble with rates drawn from a fixed amplitude band; the state then ages on a wall-clock timer before the craft is declared lost.

constants.name: Gravity acceleration
constants.unit: world units per second squared along the local vertical, added once per update

constants.name: Tumble velocity share
constants.unit: 1/second applied to the whole velocity vector when attitude control is lost, once per update

constants.name: Tumble seed angle limit
constants.unit: radians of residual angular rate below which the random tumble seed is applied; static, no timestep

constants.name: Tumble seed horizontal amplitude
constants.unit: angular rate units added per update by the tumble seed on the pitch and yaw axes

constants.name: Tumble seed vertical amplitude
constants.unit: angular rate units added per update by the tumble seed on the roll axis

constants.name: Tumble state timeout
constants.unit: seconds of elapsed game time before the tumbling state is declared lost; static timeout, evaluated with the 0.01-0.1 s frame step

capabilities: body-space gravity rotated into the local frame
thrust along the model forward axis
attitude-fed lateral acceleration
quadratic per-component velocity drag
random tumble seed bounded by residual angular rate
wall-clock timeout on the lost-control state

cards.name: Impact bands
cards.summary: Contact with terrain splits into a light touch, a glancing scrape and a fatal hit, sorted by the closing speed along the surface normal.
cards.behavior: Every surface contact is decomposed into a component along the surface normal and a tangential remainder, both taken as magnitudes from the incoming velocity vector. Above a high normal-speed threshold the model switches straight into its destroyed state, clears the thrust flag, forces the two stored impact rates to a large value and stops accepting input. Between a mid and a high threshold the craft keeps flying but the contact is recorded as a glancing scrape with small restitution factors applied to the normal and tangential parts. Below the mid threshold a second check compares the normal and tangential magnitudes: when the normal component is small but the tangential speed is large, the contact turns into a spin and the two components are stored as the spin rates that drive the visual tumble; when both are small the craft simply slides and the contact type is reported upward. Landing on the ground also snaps the model onto the terrain frame and copies the terrain normal, so a slope landing settles at the local tilt rather than the world horizontal.

constants.name: Fatal closing speed
constants.unit: world units per second along the surface normal; static threshold, no timestep

constants.name: Glancing closing speed
constants.unit: world units per second along the surface normal; static threshold, no timestep

constants.name: Glancing tangential speed
constants.unit: world units per second of tangential speed; static threshold, no timestep

constants.name: Contact restitution share
constants.unit: dimensionless factor applied to the normal and tangential parts of a glancing hit; static, no timestep

capabilities: normal and tangential decomposition of a contact
three-tier impact classification
tangential speed converted into spin rates
terrain-frame snap on ground contact
contact type reported upward for scoring

cards.name: Collective lever
cards.summary: The rotor collective travels at a fixed rate per second toward full up or full down and springs back toward the middle when released.
cards.behavior: The rotor craft has an explicit lever value normalised to the unit interval. In the ground-start state the up input raises it and the down input lowers it at the same fixed rate per second, and with no input it decays at a quarter of that rate, so a released lever falls all the way to zero. In the airborne states, holding up raises it and holding down lowers it at a profile rate, but with no input the lever is actively driven back toward one half at a slower rate rather than falling to zero, which is what holds an altitude without constant input. Reaching an empty tank drops the lever branch back to the ground behaviour. The lever is clamped into the interval after every change and a copy is published for the flight model. Control axes are separately slew-limited: a raw axis is shaped by a curve and then capped at a maximum change per second, so a full-deflection flick cannot be delivered within one update. Each pilot profile carries its own handling figures, with the forward-speed reference that normalises longitudinal authority varying by roughly a third across profiles.

constants.name: Ground lever up rate
constants.unit: fraction of full lever per second, applied with the 0.01-0.1 s frame step

constants.name: Ground lever decay rate
constants.unit: fraction of full lever per second when no input is held on the ground, applied with the 0.01-0.1 s frame step

constants.name: Airborne lever rate
constants.unit: fraction of full lever per second for both the up and the down input, applied with the 0.01-0.1 s frame step

constants.name: Airborne hands-off return rate
constants.unit: fraction of full lever per second driven back toward rest, applied with the 0.01-0.1 s frame step

constants.name: Lever rest fraction
constants.unit: fraction of full lever, the hands-off target in the airborne states; static, no timestep

constants.name: Axis slew limit
constants.unit: shaped input units per second, maximum change of a control axis

constants.name: Forward speed reference
constants.unit: world units per second, used to normalise longitudinal control authority

capabilities: explicit normalised collective lever

slew-limited control axes

cards.name: Fuel burn
cards.summary: Fuel drains at a rate read from a three-point curve on the collective lever, with low-fuel and empty states and an altitude fade on authority.
cards.behavior: Fuel is stored as a fraction of a full tank. While the engine is actually drawing, the tank is reduced every update by a value looked up from a three-point curve keyed on the current collective lever and multiplied by the frame step, so a full lever burns five times faster than an idle one. Draining stops once the tank reaches zero and the fuel-use flag drops, which in turn releases the lever branch. A refill volume, present only in one class of test, restores the tank to full when the craft enters it and raises a short message. The heads-up display adds a low-fuel warning below a small remaining fraction and an empty warning at zero, each raised once per excursion and cleared when the condition resolves. Thrust authority also fades linearly to zero across a narrow band above a high altitude, so a craft that runs dry high up coasts down through the fade instead of dropping instantly.

constants.name: Idle burn rate
constants.unit: tank fraction per second at zero collective, applied with the 0.01-0.1 s frame step

constants.name: Half collective burn rate
constants.unit: tank fraction per second at half collective, applied with the 0.01-0.1 s frame step

constants.name: Full collective burn rate
constants.unit: tank fraction per second at full collective, applied with the 0.01-0.1 s frame step

constants.name: Low fuel warning fraction
constants.unit: fraction of a full tank; static threshold, no timestep

constants.name: Authority fade start altitude
constants.unit: world units of height; static threshold, no timestep

constants.name: Authority fade band
constants.unit: world units of height over which authority reaches zero; static threshold, no timestep

capabilities: fuel burn keyed on the collective lever

cards.name: Thrust burst arc
cards.summary: A hop fires along the craft nose for a fixed window and then falls ballistically, with a quarter of the local air added to the acceleration.
cards.behavior: The hopping craft integrates a velocity accumulator and a position with an explicit scheme: the accumulator takes twice the acceleration times the frame step, then the position takes twice that accumulator times the same step, so the pair reproduces the expected displacement over one step while remaining stable at both ends of the frame-step clamp. A hop starts a timer and applies an acceleration along the craft's forward vector scaled by a launch factor for the first one and a half seconds; when the window closes the forward term drops to zero and only gravity remains. Gravity uses the standard downward magnitude scaled by a per-craft factor, so heavier craft arc more tightly. The ambient air vector at the craft's position is sampled every update and a quarter of it is added to the acceleration, so a strong gust visibly bends the arc and a thermal holds the craft up. On contact the pitch angle is compared against a fixed limit, and a hit beyond either side of it abandons the glide state in favour of a tumble.

constants.name: Hop thrust window
constants.unit: seconds of powered flight after a hop, counted with the 0.01-0.1 s frame step

constants.name: Hop thrust scale
constants.unit: world units per second squared per unit of the launch factor, added once per update

constants.name: Craft gravity scale
constants.unit: world units per second squared of downward acceleration, multiplied by a per-craft factor and applied once per update

constants.name: Air field share
constants.unit: fraction of the local air velocity added to the acceleration, once per update

constants.name: Integration factor
constants.unit: dimensionless, applied to both the velocity and the position step at the 0.01-0.1 s frame step

constants.name: Contact pitch limit
constants.unit: degrees of pitch beyond which a contact starts a tumble; static limit, no timestep

capabilities: timed thrust burst along the craft nose

cards.name: Chase framing
cards.summary: A clip range, a symmetric projection box and a zoom divisor define the view, and the chase distance is clamped at both ends.
cards.behavior: The camera owns a near and far clip distance and stores the projection box as four half-extents measured at unit zoom. A zoom entry point divides the near clip by the requested zoom and rescales the four half-extents by that same ratio, so a larger zoom narrows the frustum without moving the near plane; each vehicle calls it every frame with its own zoom figure, which is how a boost widens the view. Each vehicle overrides the framing after creating its camera, and the winged craft sets a short minimum follow distance together with a long maximum. The chase mode enforces both: when the target comes closer than the minimum it pushes the eye out along the sight line, and when the target is farther than the maximum it pulls the eye in. The chase also offsets the aim point along a direction blended between the craft's back axis and the world up axis, so a level fly-past keeps ground in frame, and it adds height when the craft's altitude reading is small. The follow heading is smoothed by a rate-limited approach helper with its own rate, after being unwrapped by a full turn whenever the raw angle crosses the half-turn boundary, so the view never spins the long way round.

constants.unit: world units from the eye; static, no timestep

constants.name: Far clip distance

constants.name: Vertical half extent

constants.name: Minimum follow distance
constants.unit: world units between eye and target; static limit, no timestep

constants.name: Maximum follow distance
constants.unit: world units between eye and target; static limit, no timestep

constants.name: Follow heading rate

cards.name: Wind lean on the view
cards.summary: The camera samples the air field at the eye and tilts the view against it, so a gust reads as a lean of the horizon.
cards.behavior: After the chase mode has built the eye transform, the camera converts the local air velocity at the eye position into camera space and feeds both lateral components through a rising lookup curve. The curve maps wind magnitude to an angle, climbing from zero to five degrees over the first five units and then flattening out at fourteen and a half degrees, which keeps a very strong gust from rolling the view past a readable angle. The resulting angles are rate-limited toward their targets at one unit per second and then applied as a roll about the view axis and a pitch about the cross axis. The pitch term uses half of the roll gain, so a crosswind rolls the horizon noticeably more than it pitches it, and both angles are converted from degrees to radians immediately before the rotation. Because the same air field also drives the vehicle, the visual lean and the physical drift stay in step and a player can read the wind from the horizon.

constants.name: Lean lookup gain
constants.unit: multiplier converting camera-space air velocity into a lookup input, sampled once per update

constants.name: Pitch lean share
constants.unit: fraction of the roll lean applied to the pitch axis; static, no timestep

constants.name: Lean approach rate
constants.unit: degrees per second for both lean angles, applied with the 0.01-0.1 s frame step

constants.name: Degrees to radians
constants.unit: radians per degree, applied to each lean angle once per update

constants.name: Lean curve saturation
constants.unit: degrees of lean at the flat end of the lookup curve; static table entry, no timestep

capabilities: air field sampled in camera space

cards.name: Ring gate pass
cards.summary: A pass scores only when the craft is inside the ring radius and crosses from the back face to the front face.
cards.behavior: Rings come in five size classes with a fixed size per class, and only rings that are active for the current course segment and not yet consumed are considered. For each candidate the code takes the three-dimensional distance from the craft to the ring centre and requires it to be under that ring's stored size, so the test volume is a sphere rather than a flat disc and a craft can trigger it slightly off the plane. It then projects the same offset onto the ring's own face normal: a positive projection records the current time as the front-side stamp, a negative projection records it as the back-side stamp. A gate is consumed only when the recorded front time is later than the recorded back time, which means the craft actually travelled through the opening instead of brushing the rim from the inside. Rings set to accept a crossing in either direction are satisfied once both stamps exist. On consumption the code picks a sound pitch from the ring's score type, advances the ordered child chain and hands the remaining count to the heads-up display, so a gate that opens another gate also extends the chain.

constants.name: Smallest ring size
constants.unit: world units of radius for the smallest gate class; static, no timestep

constants.name: Middle ring size
constants.unit: world units of radius for the middle gate class; static, no timestep

constants.name: Largest ring size
constants.unit: world units of radius for the largest gate class; static, no timestep

constants.name: Unstamped crossing sentinel
constants.unit: seconds of elapsed game time, standing for a side that was never crossed; static sentinel, no timestep

constants.name: Ring score pitch step
constants.unit: dimensionless sound-pitch step per score type, applied once when the gate is consumed

capabilities: five fixed ring size classes
sphere test around the ring centre

cards.name: Air volumes
cards.summary: Wind zones and thermal columns are evaluated per point and summed with a wandering ambient breeze and a map-edge breeze into one air velocity.
cards.behavior: Local wind zones come in three shapes selected by a stored index: a box around one point, a box spanned by two points, and a sphere around one point whose radius is taken from a stored vector's length. A point outside the zone contributes nothing, and the box forms reject early on each axis. Inside, a normalised distance from the zone origin selects a falloff profile: flat everywhere, linear in distance, linear in the square of distance, or flat up to eight tenths of the radius and then falling to zero at the edge. The contribution is the zone's stored wind direction scaled by that profile. Thermal columns add a vertical lift that falls off as the square root of the remaining radial fraction and that fades again over two vertical bands near the bottom and the top of the column, plus a swirl component that reverses across the column mid-line and peaks at half the radius. The composition samples the wind zones, the thermal columns, a slowly wandering ambient breeze and a map-edge term that grows linearly over a fixed band outside the playable bounds up to a fixed maximum speed at the outside of that band.

constants.name: Edge breeze band width
constants.unit: world units beyond the map bounds over which the edge breeze ramps; static, no timestep

cards.name: Medal thresholds
cards.summary: Each test is worth up to one hundred points, and a class total must clear three fixed thresholds for bronze, silver and gold.
cards.behavior: Every class and vehicle pairing keeps one point slot per test. A test that was never attempted is stored with a sentinel value that is read back as zero, so an unplayed test cannot inflate a total and a partly played set can never reach the top medal. The class total sums the per-test values for that vehicle, so a class with three tests tops out at three hundred points. The medal check walks three stored thresholds in ascending order for the chosen class and stops at the first threshold the total has not reached; that index is the medal and the difference is the points still needed. When all three thresholds are cleared the result is the top medal and the remaining-points figure becomes the gap to a full one hundred points per test. One vehicle instead scores a four-target test in which each target awards a fixed maximum, so a perfect run of all four targets is the only route to the top medal for that vehicle and a single perfect target raises a dedicated message.

constants.name: Bronze threshold
constants.unit: points of class total; static threshold, no timestep

constants.name: Silver threshold
constants.unit: points of class total; static threshold, no timestep

constants.name: Gold threshold
constants.unit: points of class total; static threshold, no timestep

constants.name: Perfect test value
constants.unit: points per test, used to size the top-medal gap; static, no timestep

constants.name: Unplayed test sentinel
constants.unit: raw per-test point slot, dimensionless sentinel that is read back as zero

constants.name: Perfect single target score
constants.unit: points awarded by one target in the four-target test; static, no timestep

capabilities: one point slot per class and test
unplayed sentinel read back as zero
three ascending medal thresholds
top-medal gap measured per test
four-target perfect run detection
